strongest_frame: s3-shot-2 creek-plan closer, 15.32 to 17.61 s (authored clock). The larger empty car, its pale roof glass showing two bare dark seats, lifts off the bank edge with its dark shadow sliding away onto a pale halo. Long current stripes overtake it as it is carried under the oak crown, over the ledge slab and out of frame before the cut.
weakest_frame: The s3 lift itself, about 15.24 to 15.93 s. In code the visible lift cue is a 10 percent scale rise (.60 to .66) plus a shadow offset of 4 to 40 px. The shadow is partly covered by the pale halo drawn on top of it, so only a crescent about 25 to 31 plan px wide stays dark at full lift. This is the cue most likely to remain subtle at 270 px.
notes: Phone-scope risks, non-blocking at code scope:

(1) Halo over the shadow. My pivot-34 note 4(b) put the halo after the shadow, so at full lift only a crescent about 25 to 31 plan px wide of the dark shadow shows down and right of the halo. If the phone again reports no separating shadow, the one-line fix is to draw the halo BEFORE the shadow so the full dark ellipse reads, offset by 40 px.
(2) Scale. .60 to .66 is the same 10 percent relative growth that round 34 could not see at .50 to .55. The lift cue now rests mainly on the shadow offset.

(3) Cabin against the roof sensor. The dome's dark plinth (x -98 to 14, y ±40, #2A3036) is drawn after the cabin. The dark seat backs (x 4 to 30) and headrests (x -6 to 6) now touch or lie under it, so the seats and plinth may merge into one dark mass around the white dome. That is round 34's 'dark panel with a round sensor'. If it does, start the seat backs and headrests at x 22 or more, or lighten the plinth when cabin > 0.
(4) At the cut the collar and shadow touch shot 2's right edge (the builder reports 3 px over). The body is inside.
(5) Exit speed is about 22 px per frame.

story_review.one_viewing_summary: Intended chain, read from code and not observed: the empty-wheel airport arrival; the table map closes the limited area; from above, a larger empty car with a pale glass roof showing two bare seats stands in shallow flood water at the creek's limestone bank edge while foam swells against it; closer, it grows and rises off a separate dark shadow onto a pale halo and is swept past the oak and the ledge and out of frame as long current stripes overtake it; the stranded street car with hazards; the desk record, the grid and the stamp; the ground-level slow roll into standing water with 'may' lit; the remedy row stamped Under development; the wet-lot tag and April 20 checks; the open curb door beside the remedy card.
story_review.opening_to_ending: The opening question asks what the federal record says about the flood problem now that the airport ride is open. The close answers it: the open curb door beside 'The remedy is currently under development'. No repair, speed, depth, parking or outcome is invented.
story_review.weakest_transition: s2 to s3 at 13.03 s. The angled table map cuts to an overhead creek with a different car, carried by 'In April' and the disclosure chip.
